summary: Adds an email search filter to the users index, a self-service profile update endpoint and a user destroy endpoint. It also adds an after_save callback that sends a welcome email.

findings.title: SQL injection in user email search
findings.problem: The index action puts params[:q] straight into the SQL text of the where clause. Any authenticated caller controls that value.
findings.consequence: An authenticated caller can inject SQL to read columns such as api_token or admin flags. The caller could also change rows in the database.
findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Any user can delete any other user
findings.problem: The before_action on line 2 exempts destroy from require_admin. The destroy action then looks up any user by params[:id] without a scope.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated user can delete every account, including admin accounts.
findings.fix: Remove destroy from the require_admin exception list so only admins reach this action.

findings.title: Mass assignment lets users grant themselves admin
findings.problem: The profile action permits every attribute in params[:user] without a filter. The User model has admin and api_token attributes that the authentication and admin checks trust.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated user can set admin to true and gain admin access. The same user can also overwrite their api_token.
findings.fix: Permit only the profile fields users may edit, such as email.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The model registers send_welcome_email as an after_save callback. Rails runs after_save on every update as well as on create.
findings.consequence: Each profile update sends the user another welcome email. That includes the new profile endpoint.
findings.fix: Register the callback with after_create_commit so it runs once, after the record is committed.

findings.title: New endpoints have no covering tests
findings.problem: The change adds search, profile and destroy behaviour and a mailer callback. The repository has no tests that exercise any of them.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization and email behaviour will go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add request tests for search, profile and destroy, and add a model test for the welcome email callback.
